ambiguities.text: The specification states 'least significant 11 bits from the first 3 16-bit words' but the endianness of word interpretation is not explicitly stated.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume big-endian byte interpretation consistent with Ethereum's general big-endian conventions for hashes. Bytes at indices (0,1), (2,3), (4,5) form the 16-bit words.

ambiguities.text: The false positive rate of the bloom filter is not documented.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume standard bloom filter false positive behavior. With 2048 bits and 3 hash functions per entry, false positive rate increases with number of entries. This is a tradeoff inherent to bloom filters.

implicit_assumptions.description: The keccak256 hash function is assumed to provide sufficiently uniform distribution for bloom filter bit positions.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Non-uniform hash distribution could cause bloom filter clustering, increasing false positive rates and degrading log query performance.

implicit_assumptions.description: The bloom filter assumes log addresses and topics are valid 20-byte and 32-byte values respectively.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Malformed input data could produce unexpected bloom patterns, though the hash function would still process any byte sequence.

implicit_assumptions.description: Clients using bloom filters for log queries must perform full log verification after bloom pre-filtering due to false positives.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Relying solely on bloom filter matches without verification could return incorrect query results.
